Maya L.: quick thread — thinking about a graceful "occupancy shedding" mode for the KV/prefix cache. goal: keep tail latency for critical tenants while shedding non-critical residency when GPU memory is tight.
Diego R.: +1. does this mean we evict more aggressively for low-priority tenants? how do we avoid oscillation?
Priya S.: we need to be careful: prefix ownership + soft-evict states can create read-after-write gaps if a writer assumes residency. leases/guards matter.
Sam (oncall): also watch the slow-path pressure. if we shed aggressively we’ll spike downstream fetches and overload the datastore.
Maya L.: thinking policy with soft/hard watermarks and timed grace: soft -> degrade to readonly residency (keep metadata/KV index cached), hard -> evict payload entirely. soft has grace_seconds to allow short bursts.
Diego R.: scoring proposal: score = access_freq * tenant_weight / (resident_bytes ^ alpha). evict lowest score. soft-evict just reduces score multiplier so it’s a lighter footprint.
Priya S.: important: when we transition from soft->hard, the owner node must publish a short-lived tombstone or fence token so readers know to refetch, not read stale in-flight KV cache. else we risk correctness bugs.
Maya L.: agree. candidate state machine:
`RESIDENT -> SOFT_EVICT (keep keys, drop value buffer) -> HARD_EVICT (remove key)`. transitions annotated with epoch token and optional tombstone timestamp.
Sam (oncall): ops question: how do we surface this in console? per-tenant shed events and an occupancy timeline. alert if hard-evict rate > X/min.
Diego R.: also consider tenant fold: small tenants folded into a shared cold slab with probabilistic read penalty. reduces bookkeeping cost.
Priya S.: locking: handoff race if node A decides to soft-evict meanwhile node B becomes owner for same prefix. need idempotent demote ops and a small compare-and-apply using lease-epoch.
Maya L.: agree. plan: (1) spike: implement soft-evict flag in cache entry + tombstone write path; (2) simulate workload in chaos harness with surge + cold-start; (3) gather latency/callvolume and datastore QPS.
Sam (oncall): I'll add dashboards: soft_evictions/sec, hard_evictions/sec, post-evict fetch latency distro, tenant_qos_violation_count. ops-bot will also emit events.
ops-bot: note: added ephemeral metric stream for testing: `metrics/occupancy_shed/test-stream` (expires in 12h) :white_check_mark:
Diego R.: one more tradeoff — soft-evict increases memory fragmentation (many small entries droppped). we should consider slab compaction run after churn windows.
Priya S.: and testcases: RYW (read-your-write) across soft demote windows, concurrent handoff + demote, tombstone expiry race. we’ll need unit tests + an integration fuzz harness.
Maya L.: volunteers for the spike? Diego + Sam? I can own proto and telemetry. Priya, can you draft the safety invariants we need to prove for RYW?
Priya S.: yep, will write invariants and a small litmus test list by EOD tomorrow.
Diego R.: happy to spike this week. I'll start with the scoring + soft eviction prototype.
Sam (oncall): I'll wire dashboards and add chaos scenarios to the canary runbook.
Maya L.: awesome. tagging follow-ups: + implement tombstone+epoch in cache proto, + simulation harness change, + telemetry and console panels. sync in 48h. :thumbsup:
